newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans turn higher on short covering, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans turn higher on short covering, funds.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures turned higher in late trade on short covering ahead of the weekend, pit sources said.
Funds were key buyers, led by Merrill Lynch, they said.

Weather was also cited as a factor. Forecasts called for rain in the western Corn Belt this weekend but traders said there was some talk of potential crop damage if the rains missed dry patches of central Illinois and eastern Iowa.
"If it doesn't rain this weekend we could be in a lot of trouble," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter. "We could be sharply higher Monday so people want to cover their shorts ahead of the weekend."
Soybeans had traded lower most of the session on a lower-than-expected weekly crush figure and on weak cash basis levels.
Traders said Merrill Lynch bought one million bushels November. Trade in the July and August was said to be very thin and volatile.
At 1233 CDT, soybeans were up five to two cents per bushel with July up five at $7.84.
